text:
elaine: Quick heads-up — marigold30b quant pass (static int4 build) on canary. Perf looks good but stress-run with max_new_tokens=512 triggered OOMs on 2/8 GPUs. Sharing notes and logs.
conor: logs?
elaine: snippet: ```RuntimeError: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory (allocation 1.2 GiB)
...line@inference: alloc_scratch -> cudamalloc -> failed``` Also driver messages show repeated heap churn / 'cuda free fragmentation' warnings.
tian: Did you try lowering prefetch or disabling KV warmup? Those warmup flows can cause slot churn under int4.
elaine: Prefetch=3, kv_warmup=enabled. On previous int8 runs we didn't see this pattern. Suspect int4 kernels + allocator freelist interaction.
rachel: What were batching settings? microbatch, dynamic window, concurrency?
elaine: batch_size=1 (per-request), dynamic batching window=30ms, microbatch cap=8, concurrent sessions ~130 during stress. OOMs correlate with spikes in concurrent long-context sessions.
mark: Hypothesis: int4 reduces steady-state tensors but increases ephemeral scratch/temporary allocations and causes freelist fragmentation when many evictions happen. Proposals: 1) lower default max_new_tokens from 512 -> 256, 2) reduce prefetch to 1, 3) enable earlier KV-trim heuristic (trim before allocation spike).
elaine: I'll run a quick canary with those three changes.
ops-bot: Canary deploy created marigold30b-quant-v2 on p-gpu-canary-7 (id: cg-774) — rolling traffic 5%.
tian: Also try toggling allocator trim frequency: export MALLOC_TRIM_THRESHOLD_=64 and enable cuda mempool trimming (cuMemPoolTrim) where supported. That reduced fragmentation in other models.
elaine: Ran two runs: runA (defaults) -> reproducible OOM at ~2.2k concurrent tokens; runB (max_new_tokens=256, prefetch=1, kv_trim=early, allocator-trim=yes) -> no OOM across 10k requests, P90 latency +3% but stable.
conor: Nice. Any measurable quality delta from the int4 quantization + these config changes?
elaine: Ran eval suite (generation + targeted QA prompts): BLEU-like score ~unchanged, top-1 token perplexity +0.8% (within our allowable regression window). No hallucination spike.
rachel: OK. Are we comfortable changing the per-route default max_new_tokens for marigold30b to 256?
mark: I'm good with that as a conservative default for hosted. Keep override for dedicated/private customers and add guidance in the docs.
elaine: I'll open PR to update onboarding notes + console defaults. Also adding an ops playbook: if heap-churn seen, flip prefetch->1, enable kv_trim early, lower max_new_tokens.
tian: I'll add allocator/freelist gauges to tracing and a histogram for 'evictions per second' so we can alert before OOMs.
elaine: Created ticket INF-1892 with the canary results, commands, and next actions. Will follow up with PR and a short postmortem if anything regresses. Thanks all :pray:
conor: Great work — let's keep the canary on 5% for 24h and monitor allocator metrics.
elaine: Ack, leaving it. Will post results tomorrow.
